$comment: Canonical framework patch set. pnpm only honors patchedDependencies at the app/workspace root, so these ship inside @octane-xplat/cli and downstream apps materialize them via `xplat patches apply` (copies files into <app>/patches/ + merges the yaml block). `pnpm sync:patches` generates the config package's patch files and the template config; `pnpm check:patches` fails on drift. Maintain a patch with `pnpm patch <specifier>` + `pnpm patch-commit` — the root workspace yaml points here so commit writes land in this dir. Entries with `template: false` target repo-internal environments (e.g. the windows preview matrix) and are omitted from the starter's patchedDependencies — pnpm fails install on declared-but-unused patches.

patches.why: Published 0.16.3 includes universal Children normalization, descriptorChildren and their compiler allowlist entries, plus compiler-owned generic binding bags. Retains universal signal-read tracking and local hooks, root event-error forwarding, the complete universal imperative-ref lifecycle, the Descriptor declaring-owner reader fallback, and the signal-owner/enclosingOwner chain so child reads reuse instance declarations. Preserves keyed component ownership through compiler-generated transparent root slots so native map reorders retain host identity, state, and portal content. Rebased against the registry 0.16.3 tarball; upstream Children and binding-bag implementations are preserved.
patches.dropWhen: An octane release (0.15.0+) exports universal Children normalization and descriptorChildren and accepts both in the universal compiler, integrates universal signal reads/local hooks and owner ancestry, forwards uncaught event-handler errors, and supports optional/replaced/nested imperative refs with callback cleanup. Generic binding bags must also participate in transaction-fragment parent rehoming. Universal array reconciliation must also preserve component keys through transparent root-slot wrappers.

patches.why: Published 9.1.3 ships the #11446 nested-tab-frame lifecycle fix and iOS explicit-size flex alignment, so those hunks are removed. Retains the unshipped parent-padding measure-spec fix and Android explicit-size flex alignment, iOS continuous corner clipping, CSS @layer cascade support, custom Android variable-font weight mapping, and percentage translate parsing, native view, and animation support. Verified against the registry 9.1.3 tarball; it has no Windows implementation, so the separate Windows preview patch remains.
patches.dropWhen: A published @nativescript/core release contains the remaining flexbox measure/alignment, continuous corners, cascade layers, custom Android variable-font weight mapping, and percentage-translate fixes (NativeScript/NativeScript#11481).

patches.why: @nativescript/vite serializes bundled CSS and dev app.css through reworkcss `css`@3.0.0, which mis-parses @layer into garbage selectors — rules die before reaching _populateRules. Adds atlayer() covering block and statement forms. Applies to a transitive dep — no app declares it directly.
patches.dropWhen: npm `css` is unmaintained — drop when @nativescript/vite's serializer stops using it (e.g. pointed at NS's vendored css/lib/parse; NativeScript#11462)

patches.why: Remaining dev-server fixes on @nativescript/vite 8.0.20: classify only the requested vendor entry under active native ESM conditions, keeping mixed source-root/compiled-subpath packages on the Vite transform path; collect re-export specifiers in the .vite/deps rewrite; route outside-roots /@fs paths through /ns/m; probe non-active platform and native suffixes; redirect bare octane to octane/universal/native in deps-bundle esbuild passes; give library files served per-module on first boot static /ns/m vendor imports so ESM evaluation order and live bindings hold, keeping package-internal non-entry files concrete instead of folding them onto the package root (first-boot `Class extends value …` in gesturehandler); canonicalize /@fs pnpm virtual-store paths onto the vendor route's `/ns/m/node_modules/<pkg>` spelling when the store and root-resolved package share a realpath, so a package's modules can't split into two registries (first-boot `is not a registered element` in octane's element registry); add .mobile to tsconfig-paths and generated checker suffixes; scan the app-local pnpm virtual store for served node_modules URLs; ignore per-package turbo.json as workspace markers; resolve # package-imports specifiers in served-module rewrites; preserve, compile, and hot-update virtual stylesheets (NativeScript#11551); and inspect ESM export declarations/specifiers for native default-import validation instead of matching comments, strings, or a narrow export syntax (NativeScript#11566). Shared-source graph and hot-context IDs now use the same app/workspace/@fs paths as served imports, preserving distinct roots (NativeScript#11569); extensionless workspace requests probe filesystem-anchored extension/platform candidates so hot reimports can fetch shared modules (NativeScript#11570). Linked-checkout discovery and candidate anchoring shipped in 8.0.20 (NativeScript#11559), so those local hunks are removed. Vite `resolve.alias` entries are captured in configResolved and replayed inside the NativeScript esbuild passes (deps bundle, vendor bundle) via an esbuild alias plugin with @rollup/plugin-alias semantics, so Vite resolve.alias redirects for packages that are not installed (e.g. the renderer's full-MasonKit imports mapped to Mason core) resolve to real files instead of throw-on-evaluate optional-dependency stubs, while installed packages keep their default resolution; presence ignores pnpm's hidden `.pnpm/node_modules` hoist, so another workspace app's hoisted copy (apps/windows' full MasonKit) does not disable the alias; the deps-bundle disk cache key fingerprints the captured aliases. The runtime-plugin bare-specifier fold locates a package's package.json through Node's node_modules ancestor chain instead of a literal projectRoot/node_modules join, so deep `pkg/dist/...` specifiers fold back to the bare vendor id in hoisted workspaces where the app's own node_modules is empty (a missed fold leaves the vendor registry without the specifier and device require resolves a module missing the vendored exports). The bare-specifier HTTP fallback anchors at the importer's real path and walks its node_modules ancestors when the spec is absent from the app root chain, so a package present only as an importer's pnpm sibling (storybook's @storybook/global) rewrites to a serving /ns/m/@fs URL instead of the root-resolved /ns/m/node_modules/<spec> 404. The ALWAYS_INCLUDE presence check walks the filesystem node_modules ancestors instead of require.resolve, so NODE_PATH injected by pnpm bin shims cannot expose the hidden `.pnpm/node_modules` hoist and collect a package the app does not actually have (stacktrace-js via the workspace's firebase-crashlytics).
patches.dropWhen: Upstream classifies requested vendor entries under active ESM conditions (including mixed source-root/compiled-subpath exports), and ships the remaining re-export, outside-roots /@fs, platform/native candidate, deps-bundle alias, .mobile suffix (checker: NativeScript#11480), app-local pnpm store, turbo.json workspace-marker, # package-imports, virtual stylesheet fixes (NativeScript#11551), accurate default-export link validation (NativeScript#11566), shared-source HMR identity preservation (NativeScript#11569), extensionless workspace fetching (NativeScript#11570), main-realm package-internal file preservation (upstream fixed only the worker realm), and pnpm virtual-store /@fs canonicalization onto vendor-route URLs. Upstream esbuild dev passes honor Vite resolve.alias. Upstream resolves installed package metadata through ancestor node_modules for the exports reverse map.

patches.why: Driver treats a prop dropped from an update's complete prop bag — or set to `undefined`/`null` — as a removal and restores the documented default: Property/CssProperty setters get `unsetValue`, plain fields restore the captured pre-prop value, and applied `style` keys diff per key. A never-applied `undefined` still skips the write since NativeScript native setters coerce it (e.g. editable → ios.userInteractionEnabled = NO). Aligns intrinsic ref types with Octane callback cleanup and nested arrays with optional entries. Advertises the implemented visibility capability so committed suspense bodies can be retained while pending. Preserves authored Grid row/col/span metadata independently of NativeScript defaults and computed auto-placement, notifying Grid when placement props change.
patches.dropWhen: @nativescript-community/octane ships removal-reset prop semantics, the undefined-skip, visibility capability, Octane-compatible intrinsic ref types, and Grid authored placement metadata with change notifications upstream.

patches.why: Retains the workspace's NativeScript driver fixes when upgrading to 0.2.5 for portal support: a prop dropped from an update's complete prop bag — or set to `undefined`/`null` — is a removal that restores the documented default (Property/CssProperty setters get `unsetValue`, plain fields the captured pre-prop value, `style` keys diff per key); a never-applied `undefined` still skips the write. Synced with PR #14: registered setters are identified before resetting (ordinary fields never receive the sentinel), inline removal refreshes matching class CSS through the isolated core 9.1 `_cssState.onChange` hook, CSS variables use public removal, strings use the core CSS parser, and replacement views capture fresh defaults. Also advertises the implemented visibility capability, carries Octane callback ref types, and preserves authored Grid row/col/span metadata. Hosts custom-layout containers (e.g. MasonKit ViewBase) that own child lists via insertChild/removeChild/getChildrenCount without subclassing LayoutBase. Additionally, the masonry cutover: masonview resolves to MasonKit View and scrollview to MasonKit Scroll as the only layout containers, with zero layout props — every former prop name warns-and-drops and all CSS semantics arrive through the style bag; foreign native leaves mirror resolved class and inline layout styles through Style.fromView, observe longhand changes and native recreation, and explicitly clear removed placement — removal restores the CSS cascade, so a later sibling attachment cannot resurrect removed tracks. Container alignment uses the core stretch default without a local style override, allowing class-authored centering. Inline style resets reapply the matching CSS cascade. Re-exports Octane's ClassValue unchanged and stringifies truthy numeric class values while omitting 0 and NaN, matching Octane 0.11. Maps collapsed foreign native leaves to Mason display:none, restoring effective display on visibility changes so both layout hosts omit the same item (#45). Adds observeBatches(): willApply/didApply batch observers on every NativeScript root (including nested applies, with depth) so layout projection can snapshot before and commit after each host batch, which a rerender-driven signal cannot cover on keyed reorder.
patches.dropWhen: The upstream driver hosts Mason containers, preserves removal-reset semantics, and synchronizes resolved foreign-leaf layout styles with class/inline precedence and native-view lifecycle support. Foreign leaf visibility must also remove collapsed items from Mason layout and restore their effective display. Upstream ships a batch observer.

patches.why: octaneServerStrategy's SCRIPT_FILE_RE only covers [jt]sx? — .tsrx edits never emit the deferred ns:hmr-delta broadcast, so component HMR silently never reaches the device. Also counts open /ns-hmr sockets so the update summary stops reporting recipients=0 for delivered updates. Includes shared script sources in transaction ordering while excluding dependencies, tests and declarations. External-source edits use the absolute source for graph identity and a Vite /@fs transform URL instead of treating parent-relative paths as app URLs.
patches.dropWhen: vite-octane release adds .tsrx matching and uses canonical graph IDs with filesystem transform URLs for external sources

patches.why: Windows preview abae298 from NativeScript#11272 uses Vite 8.0.21. Retains /ns/m re-export records, outside-root /@fs routing through the device transform, and .mobile-aware tsconfig-paths probing. Vendor-manifest gating and percent-decoded module paths are now upstream and no longer patched. Carries the 8.0.20 vendor collector repair for Android linked-source consumers (#51): classify the selected native export, excluding source roots even when sibling exports are compiled and preserving compiled subpaths and native plugins.
patches.dropWhen: windows moves off the preview pin — the real fix lands upstream with the windows platform merge (NativeScript#11272/#11468); retain the vendor collector repair until an adopted upstream release classifies the requested export under the native bundler conditions.

patches.why: Windows preview abae298 from NativeScript#11272 retains CSS @layer cascade machinery and explicit-size flex alignment, Windows pointer subscription and hover ownership, cancellation/capture-loss handling and gesture separation, parent-driven percentage sizing lifecycle and padded content-box updates, raw keyDown/keyUp subscription ownership, submit cancellation, and input focus/blur ownership, IsEnabled forwarding, accessible names, secure readonly, and literal non-CSS property values. Also moves _ensureNativeTransforms into a leaf module to break the view-common/animation import cycle that crashed ESM bundle evaluation at startup. The #11446 frame/tab fixes are now upstream and removed. Preserves upstream transparent-background hit testing and contact-only pointer moves. Registry core 9.1.4-next.0 has no Windows implementation; this patch targets the commit-pinned preview with that version. Uses the explicit NSWinRT.dotnet.invoke bridge for synchronous existence, recursive directory creation, and nontruncating OpenOrCreate file creation, preserving Core's System import shim. Existence projection failures are not treated as missing paths. Adds Windows single-contact pan with cumulative logical-DIP deltas, owned pointer capture, cancellation, and cleanup while retaining sibling touch delivery. Exposes the shared native event subscription registry through __xplatWindowsEvents so optional leaves reuse the host owner without deep-importing a second core module.
patches.dropWhen: A published Windows-capable core contains the retained cascade, layout, pointer, input, and filesystem repairs. Source repairs remain in tools/platform-qualification/patches/windows-pointer-core.patch, tools/platform-qualification/patches/windows-layout/core-percent-source.patch, tools/platform-qualification/patches/windows-input-core.patch, tools/platform-qualification/patches/windows-module-cycle.patch, and tools/platform-qualification/patches/windows-keyboard/. Filesystem artifact repair and qualification boundaries are recorded in .agents/docs/parity/windows-support-progress.md. The release must also emit cumulative Windows pan deltas with capture-loss cancellation and lifecycle cleanup; bounded x64 mouse evidence and remaining hardware-touch gates are in .agents/docs/parity/windows-support-progress.md.

patches.why: Enables `resolveHiddenExtensions` on the language plugin's typescript facet so extensionless specifiers (e.g. './Text') probe `.tsrx` after moduleSuffixes — required for a single extensionless shared barrel to resolve per-platform leaves under tsrx-tsc and the IDE plugin.
patches.dropWhen: @tsrx/typescript-plugin sets resolveHiddenExtensions in its typescript facet upstream

patches.why: useEditor.ts reads bare process.env.NODE_ENV — no node global exists in the harness typecheck program. Adds a module-local process declaration for typecheck. (The './Context' self-import half of the 0.0.51 patch shipped upstream in 0.0.52 via octanejs/octane#1502.)
patches.dropWhen: @octanejs/tiptap declares process ambiently in useEditor.ts (closed unmerged upstream) or the leaf stops typechecking its raw sources

patches.why: @nativescript/doctor's Android runtime check reads the app's raw devDependencies specifier and npm dist-tag resolves anything that isn't a semver range — a pnpm `catalog:` pin throws 'The determined Android runtime version ... is not valid' and kills `ns build android` before toolchain checks. Resolve catalog specifiers through the installed package's manifest, reusing the existing tgz-branch mechanism.
patches.dropWhen: @nativescript/doctor resolves non-registry specifiers (catalog:, workspace:, link:) to the installed package version, or nativescript stops gating `ns build` on it.
